title: Any Claude Code skills you’d recommend for building a 3D game from scratch?
author: owen800q
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I’m planning to build a 3D game from scratch with AI assistance. I currently have **both Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions**, and I also plan to use **GPT Image 2.5 to design assets and create concept art**.

Are there any **Claude Code skills, plugins, MCP servers, or workflows** you’d recommend for this?

I haven’t picked an engine yet, so I’m open to Unity, Unreal, Godot, or other suggestions. I’m mainly looking for help with:

* Project setup and code organization
* Player movement, cameras, physics, and gameplay mechanics
* Debugging and testing
* Designing assets and bringing them into the game engine
* Keeping the project maintainable as it grows

If you’ve used a similar setup, how would you split tasks between Claude Code, ChatGPT, and image generation? I’d also love advice on turning AI-generated concept art into usable 3D assets—I know generating an image isn’t the same as creating a game-ready model.

My goal is a **small, playable prototype**, not a huge game. Any recommended skills, repos, tutorials, or examples would be appreciated. Thanks!

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Just a heads up but the Unity MCP is deprecated, it’s recommended to use the Unity CLI binary and the Unity Pipeline package instead of that to drive the Unity Editor from the terminal.

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: Can you link me any documentation on that? I have been using the Unity MCP with success for months included extensively today. Always open to improving my workflow though.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body:
https://unity.com/resources/unity-pipeline-cli-technical-walkthrough

Sure thing, this goes over all of its capabilities as well as how to set it up.

From my personal experience using both, it consumes less tokens than using the MCP.

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: Apparently I am already using CLI and Unity Pipeline Package and I’m simply an idiot haha … thank you.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Lol! No problem, you were up to date and didn't even realize it.

comments.author: MichaelEmouse
comments.body:
I created my first half dozen prototypes in Claude Chat.



Claude Code is far ahead for coding. ChatGPT for image generation.

  
Blender MCP add-on.

  
I've tried the free versions of Hunyuan, Tripo, Rodin and Meshy. Meshy seemed far better. You can use image generation AI then feed that image to an image-to-3D model AI.

  
Meshy turned this image into the model I'll add next:

https://i.redd.it/gexshy90bjyh1.jpeg

replies.author: MichaelEmouse
replies.body:
What would be an efficient number of faces for this?

  
I can't say I've learned to use 3D model generation in a way that's compute-efficient.

replies.author: anon999387
replies.body: Look up retopology. Anything with millions of faces will crush performance.

replies.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
replies.body: To add to this. Argon is the king of 3D animation when you combine it with Blender MCP.

comments.author: elimit
comments.body: Just talk to Claude dude, he’ll tell you what you need to know

comments.author: forgingtheflow
comments.body: I think my claude has just the blender MCP, but I don’t use it for models anymore, I use ChatGPT for models and artwork. Coding and planning is Claude.

comments.author: s22stumarket
comments.body:
I am doing this for few weeks.
Haven't found skills that have given a difference.

My tip is to greate a skill/instruction that puts all decisions in a file. Otherwise it spirals out of control, like it happened with my project.

comments.body:
